note: One argument off the small network's landed pair: r2026-11-10-6-small-video's argv and timeout character for character with --work-scale 0.75 -> 0.5 and --save-after small-ws50-after.png, entry `minimal-small` unchanged, so this run measures the pass's internal size and nothing else. It exists because the goal is 60 fps at a fixed 1440p output and an internal size behind a setting is the quality trade the goal item authorises; --work-scale is that switch and the port's resize_rgba8 does both bilinear dispatches, so no rebuild is needed. Read, in this order: (1) the worker banner's model line must read `/opt/neuralscreen/model-small` - if it reads `/opt/neuralscreen/model` nothing below counts; (2) median and steady rate against r2026-11-10-6-small-video's 24.1 ms / 41.6 fps steady at --work-scale 0.75 on this exact shape, and against the large network's 30.2 ms / 33.2 fps (r2026-11-10-5-ws-video, same shape); 60 fps needs 16.7 ms, so a frame near 17-19 ms means this one argument has taken most of the remaining gap, while a frame that barely moves means the fixed costs (readback + reply at the frame size, plus the client chain) are the floor and the internal size is spent; (3) the artifact `small-ws50-after.png` must be 2560x1440 RGBA (colortype 6) - anything at 1280x720 means the pass's upscale back to the frame size did not happen; (4) it must differ from r2026-11-10-6-small-video's published frame `runs/done/r2026-11-10-6-small-video/small-ws-after.png` - a different internal size must move the picture, so identical bytes mean the resize never ran and the reading is void; report the mean absolute difference and the share of pixels moved. Card gate as always: read gpu_before / gpu_after and idle_waited_s out of the report, quote the spread beside the median, and do not compare the two runs if a gate reads BUSY before the run or the idle wait is non-zero.
